title.narrative: Emergency and Transitional Humanitarian Support for Returnees in Eastern Zone of Tigray Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThe humanitarian crisis in Ethiopia has become complex, facing multiple challenges including conflict, violence, insecurity, climate shocks inflation. The country is also facing multiple health emergencies including cholera outbreak. These crises combined with the lingering effects of droughts conflicts have further eroded the resilience of affected communities. Food insecurity remains a central issue driven by recurrent climate shocks, low agricultural productivity soaring food prices. The Tigray region of Ethiopia continues to face a profound humanitarian crisis following years of armed conflict, displacement, and destruction of basic services. Communities in Erob, GuloMekeda and Zelambesa remain heavily affected, with women, girls, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups carrying the greatest burden. The region in general has not yet recovered from the northern Ethiopia conflict that has devastated basic services, infrastructures and has contributed to some of the humanitarian needs. The Rapid Gender Analysis conducted by CARE (June 2025) for Irob and Gulomekda shows that escalated protection risks with widespread Gender-based violence (GBV), including sexual assault, early and forced marriage, trafficking, and intimate partner violence. Women and girls are most affected, but men and boys also face detention, forced migration, and violence. Weak justice systems and limited survivor services leave communities unprotected. Access to services such as health facilities, schools, and water systems are either destroyed or non-functional is severely constrained. Essential services such as sexual and reproductive health (SRH), GBV response, and education remain largely unavailable, particularly in remote and insecure areas. Many households survive on one meal per day particularly vulnerable groups including female-headed households, child-headed households, older people, and persons with disabilities often excluded from aid distributions which has exacerbated food insecurity. Farming systems, livestock, and markets were looted or destroyed which has led to deterioration of livelihoods. Malnutrition is a critical issue in the geographical areas where the GAM rate among children lt 5 ranges between 15% to 32.8% while MAM rate among PLW the ranges between 33.4% to 43% in these woredas. ltbrgtAgainst this backdrop, CARE Ethiopia, in partnership with CRADO, will implement a targeted humanitarian response in the Eastern Zone of Tigray. The intervention will focus on ltspangtZalambesa tolt/spangtltspangtwn and lt/spangtltspangtthe woredas of Ilt/spangtltspangtrob, and Gulo Mekeda.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThis project is strategically designed to complement and add value to existing interventions by the consortium in the identified areas, while carefully avoiding duplication and resource waste backed by the rapid needs assessment conducted for all the locations. CARE is currently implementing project activities in WASH, health, nutrition, and protection sectors. To maximize impact and efficiency, project activities have been adapted to meet identified gaps: activities already covered by existing programs are deprioritized in overlapping locations, allowing the consortium to shift focus to underserved woredas.ltbrgtOverall, this response aims to address urgent humanitarian needs through the sectors of ESNFI, WASH and Agriculture while laying the foundation for safe, dignified, and sustainable solutions for returning and host communities in the affected woredas.ltbrgtlt/pgt
